place.name: Detroit — neighborhoods carry the city
place.kind: city, Michigan, USA — public posts, Sept–Oct 2026
place.summary: A city where the jobs moved to the suburbs and the neighborhoods carry what remains: local businesses, a garden teaching young men, photographers documenting the streets — under institutional strain.

readings.label: Public posts naming Detroit in the indexer window

stories.text:
so racist that they vote down measures to allow the blacks to get into their towns more easily. 

detroit is STILL a poor city and most of the jobs are in the suburbs.

you have to be able to get to work. most jobs REQUIRE "reliable transportation" which is code for have access to a car EVERY DAY.

Today was Adventures in Grocery Shopping day.  I got the wonky wheel.  Talked to a truck driver who said diesel was over $7.00 a gallon in Detroit.  I got hot dogs (not all beef), frozen meatballs, & frozen breaded chicken & tater tots & pasta, so not real food.  Too expensive.

I was having a conversation with another detroiter (and professional urbanist) about how it took longer for us to bounce back versus LA/NYC/Chi/Atl.

my thesis: post-bankruptcy PTSD. our big little city status compounded things.

data: repeated leadership job postings & new hires lasting ~1yr

#Michigan has an estimated 25,000 #Latino-owned businesses, many in southwest Detroit. A national campaign asks people to spend $30 at one before Hispanic Heritage Month ends Oct. 15. #HispanicHeritageMonth

I'm a historic tour guide here in Detroit, and my go-to answer when people ask me why things are the way they are around here is, "Capitalism, white supremacy, or (usually) both at the same time."
A large community sprang up in Detroit, which numbered from as many as 15,000 to 20,000 #Macedonian Americans by the 1980s.
A Polymarket logo recently appeared on a Detroit water tower, which the city plans to investigate for a possible permit violation.

Private emails show a Detroit Thermal employee asked a 1300 East Lafayette leader to recruit two Black residents to speak in support of its steam project. The response: “We are playing the diversity card as best as we can get that going.” www.metrotimes.com/news/playing...

signals.statement: The jobs are in the suburbs and 'reliable transportation' is the gate — distance and cost keep residents out of work.

sips.title: Transport is the jobs bottleneck
sips.what_changes: Residents name 'reliable transportation' as the gate, not skills. A transit answer unlocks the suburban jobs without moving anyone.

sips.title: Institutions compound
sips.what_changes: Each documented street, taught cohort, and opened shop raises the floor the next one starts from — the revival is the network.
